newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- OCT 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- OCT 24.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--Government economy team tested by the proposal by government ministers for an urgent 'solidarity tax' on high incomes and real estate. National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou furious at leak to press.
--T-bill interest rates to fall to 12.30 percent, following the successful bond auction, finance ministry says.
--Two more insurance companies have licences withdrawn.
IMERISIA
--ASE authorities choose the US to announce new measures for the stock exchange. In Reuters exclusive, ASE President Manolis Xanthakis says short-selling will begin on the exchange by end-1996.
--Finance ministry set to issue five-year bond with fixed interest of 10.5 percent mid-November, sources say.
--Commercial Bank sees 81 percent fall in net profits for first half 1996, attributed to delayed revenues and increased expenses.
--Papandoniou stand-off over new tax. Sources say the minister called Prime Minister Costas Simitis yesterday to tell him he's not signing any decision that will impose new taxes.
KERDOS
--Federation of Greek Industries (SEB) say new taxes will work against growth. The answer is to be found in reducing state expenditures, SEB says.
--30,000 Greek families have 7.5 trillion drachmas at their disposal, Citibank study on private banking reveals.
EXPRESS
--Flurry of rumours causes concern in government economic circles. Finance ministry goes on the defensive, saying there are no plans afoot regarding the imposition of new taxes.
--EU Commissioner Monika Wulf-Mathies concerned over Greece's low absorption rates for tourist enterprises programme.
--Development deputy minister Mihalis Chrysohoidis agrees to demands for clear and long-term operating framework for the market.
--Development minstry ready to implement Energy Business Programme, with investments of 160 billion drachmas.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--A return to foreign borrowing for the cheapest servicing of the debt. Finance ministry plans to increase its foreign borrowing and be more aggressive on interest rates in its efforts to reduce spending on debt servicing.
--Merchant marine minister Stavros Soumakis announces changes for funding and licencing in coastal shipping.
--Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
